items.title: Noun + です
items.meaning: Make a polite statement identifying or describing something.
notes: Make a polite statement identifying or describing something.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + は
items.meaning: Mark the topic that the rest of the sentence comments on.
notes: Mark the topic that the rest of the sentence comments on.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + も
items.meaning: Add that the same statement is true of another topic.
notes: Add that the same statement is true of another topic.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Sentence + か
items.meaning: Turn a polite statement into a neutral question.
notes: Turn a polite statement into a neutral question.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + の + Noun
items.meaning: Connect nouns for possession, affiliation, or description.
notes: Connect nouns for possession, affiliation, or description.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: これ・それ・あれ
items.meaning: Point to a thing near the speaker, listener, or neither person.
notes: Point to a thing near the speaker, listener, or neither person.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: この・その・あの + Noun
items.pattern: この・その・あの + Noun
items.meaning: Point to a specific noun by its relative distance.
formation: この・その・あの + Noun
notes: Point to a specific noun by its relative distance.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: ここ・そこ・あそこ
items.meaning: Point to locations near the speaker, listener, or farther away.
notes: Point to locations near the speaker, listener, or farther away.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: だれ・何・どこ・いつ
items.pattern: だれ・何・どこ・いつ
items.meaning: Ask for a person, thing, place, or time.
formation: だれ・何・どこ・いつ
notes: Ask for a person, thing, place, or time.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: あります・います
items.meaning: State that an inanimate thing or animate being exists.
notes: State that an inanimate thing or animate being exists.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: There is a teacher in the classroom.

items.title: Noun + が
items.meaning: Mark the grammatical subject, especially with existence and ability.
notes: Mark the grammatical subject, especially with existence and ability.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
examples.reading: 机の上に本があります。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: There is a book on the desk.

items.title: Place + に
items.meaning: Mark where something exists or the destination of movement.
notes: Mark where something exists or the destination of movement.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: There is a cat at home.

items.title: Time + に
items.meaning: Mark a specific time when an action occurs.
notes: Mark a specific time when an action occurs.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + から・まで
items.meaning: Mark the starting and ending point of time or place.
notes: Mark the starting and ending point of time or place.

examples.japanese: 九時から五時まで働きます。
examples.reading: 九時から五時まで働きます。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I work from nine to five.

items.title: Noun + と + Noun
items.meaning: Join nouns in a complete list meaning and.
notes: Join nouns in a complete list meaning and.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + や + Noun
items.meaning: Give representative examples from a larger list.
notes: Give representative examples from a larger list.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本やペンがあります。
examples.reading: 机の上に本やペンがあります。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: There are books, pens, and such on the desk.

items.title: Verb stem + ます
items.meaning: Express a habitual or future action politely.
notes: Express a habitual or future action politely.

examples.japanese: 毎日日本語を勉強します。
examples.reading: 毎日日本語を勉強します。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Verb stem + ません
items.meaning: Express that a present or future action does not happen.
notes: Express that a present or future action does not happen.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Verb stem + ました
items.meaning: Express a completed past action politely.
notes: Express a completed past action politely.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Verb stem + ませんでした
items.pattern: Verb stem + ませんでした
items.meaning: Express that an action did not happen in the past.
formation: Verb stem + ませんでした
notes: Express that an action did not happen in the past.

examples.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べませんでした。
examples.reading: 朝ご飯を食べませんでした。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + を + Verb
items.meaning: Mark the direct object affected by an action.
notes: Mark the direct object affected by an action.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Place + で + Verb
items.meaning: Mark the place where an action happens.
notes: Mark the place where an action happens.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Place + へ + movement verb
items.meaning: Mark the direction toward which someone moves.
notes: Mark the direction toward which someone moves.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Place + に + movement verb
items.meaning: Mark a concrete destination or arrival point.
notes: Mark a concrete destination or arrival point.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Person + と
items.meaning: Mark the person who participates in an action with someone.
notes: Mark the person who participates in an action with someone.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Tool or vehicle + で
items.meaning: Mark the means, instrument, language, or transport used.
notes: Mark the means, instrument, language, or transport used.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + をください
items.meaning: Politely ask for an item in a shop or restaurant.
notes: Politely ask for an item in a shop or restaurant.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: て-form + ください
items.meaning: Politely request that another person perform an action.
notes: Politely request that another person perform an action.

examples.japanese: ここに名前を書いてください。
examples.reading: ここに名前を書いてください。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: て-form + もいいです
items.meaning: Ask for or grant permission to do something.
notes: Ask for or grant permission to do something.

examples.japanese: 写真を撮ってもいいですか。
examples.reading: 写真を撮ってもいいですか。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: て-form + はいけません
items.meaning: State that an action is prohibited.
notes: State that an action is prohibited.

examples.japanese: ここで食べてはいけません。
examples.reading: ここで食べてはいけません。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Verb stem + ましょう
items.meaning: Invite someone to do an action together.
notes: Invite someone to do an action together.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Verb stem + ませんか
items.meaning: Invite someone politely while leaving room to decline.
notes: Invite someone politely while leaving room to decline.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: Would you like to watch a movie?

items.title: Verb stem + たいです
items.meaning: Express what the speaker wants to do.
notes: Express what the speaker wants to do.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I want to go to Japan.

items.title: Noun + がほしいです
items.meaning: Express that the speaker wants a thing.
notes: Express that the speaker wants a thing.

examples.japanese: 新しい自転車がほしいです。
examples.reading: 新しい自転車がほしいです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: い-adjective + Noun/です
items.meaning: Describe a noun or make a polite statement with an i-adjective.
notes: Describe a noun or make a polite statement with an i-adjective.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: な-adjective + な + Noun
items.meaning: Use a na-adjective before a noun or with です as a predicate.
notes: Use a na-adjective before a noun or with です as a predicate.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: くないです・ではありません
items.pattern: くないです・ではありません
items.meaning: Make i-adjectives and na-adjectives negative politely.
formation: くないです・ではありません
notes: Make i-adjectives and na-adjectives negative politely.

examples.japanese: この本は高くないです。
examples.reading: この本は高くないです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: かったです・でした
items.meaning: Describe a past state with an adjective.
notes: Describe a past state with an adjective.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: A は B より adjective
items.pattern: A は B より adjective
items.meaning: Compare A with B using B as the reference point.
formation: A は B より adjective
notes: Compare A with B using B as the reference point.

examples.japanese: 電車はバスより速いです。
examples.reading: 電車はバスより速いです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: The train is faster than the bus.

items.title: A より B のほうが adjective
items.pattern: A より B のほうが adjective
items.meaning: Say that B has more of a quality than A.
formation: A より B のほうが adjective
notes: Say that B has more of a quality than A.

examples.japanese: 肉より魚のほうが好きです。
examples.reading: 肉より魚のほうが好きです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I like fish more than meat.

items.title: Group + で + Noun + が一番
items.pattern: Group + で + Noun + が一番
items.meaning: Identify the item with the greatest degree in a group.
formation: Group + で + Noun + が一番
notes: Identify the item with the greatest degree in a group.

examples.japanese: 果物でりんごが一番好きです。
examples.reading: 果物でりんごが一番好きです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: Among fruits, I like apples best.

items.title: Noun + が好き・嫌いです
items.pattern: Noun + が好き・嫌いです
items.meaning: Express likes and dislikes toward a noun or activity.
formation: Noun + が好き・嫌いです
notes: Express likes and dislikes toward a noun or activity.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + が上手・下手です
items.pattern: Noun + が上手・下手です
items.meaning: Describe skill or lack of skill in an activity.
formation: Noun + が上手・下手です
notes: Describe skill or lack of skill in an activity.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: My younger sister is good at cooking.

items.title: Noun + が分かります
items.meaning: State that someone understands a language or fact.
notes: State that someone understands a language or fact.

examples.japanese: 少し日本語が分かります。
examples.reading: 少し日本語が分かります。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Reason + から
items.meaning: Give a simple reason for the following statement or choice.
notes: Give a simple reason for the following statement or choice.

examples.japanese: 雨ですから、家にいます。
examples.reading: 雨ですから、家にいます。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: Because it is raining, I will stay home.

items.title: Noun/Verb dictionary form + 前に
items.meaning: Place one action before another action or time.
notes: Place one action before another action or time.

examples.japanese: 寝る前に本を読みます。
examples.reading: 寝る前に本を読みます。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I read a book before sleeping.

items.title: Noun/Verb past form + 後で
items.meaning: Place an action after another event.
notes: Place an action after another event.

examples.japanese: 仕事の後で買い物します。
examples.reading: 仕事の後で買い物します。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Plain form + 時
items.meaning: Describe what happens at a particular time or situation.
notes: Describe what happens at a particular time or situation.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行く時、カメラを買いました。
examples.reading: 日本へ行く時、カメラを買いました。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: When I went to Japan, I bought a camera.

items.title: もう + past/affirmative
items.meaning: Say that an expected action has already happened.
notes: Say that an expected action has already happened.

examples.japanese: もう昼ご飯を食べました。
examples.reading: もう昼ご飯を食べました。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: まだ + negative
items.meaning: Say that an expected action has not happened yet.
notes: Say that an expected action has not happened yet.

examples.japanese: 宿題はまだ終わっていません。
examples.reading: 宿題はまだ終わっていません。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: The homework is not finished yet.

items.title: て-form + います
items.meaning: Describe an action in progress or a continuing state.
notes: Describe an action in progress or a continuing state.

examples.japanese: 今、新聞を読んでいます。
examples.reading: 今、新聞を読んでいます。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I am reading the newspaper now.

items.title: て-form + から
items.meaning: State that one action happens after another is completed.
notes: State that one action happens after another is completed.

examples.japanese: 手を洗ってから食べます。
examples.reading: 手を洗ってから食べます。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: I eat after washing my hands.

items.title: past plain + り、past plain + りします
items.pattern: past plain + り、past plain + りします
items.meaning: List representative activities without claiming a complete list.
formation: past plain + り、past plain + りします
notes: List representative activities without claiming a complete list.

examples.japanese: 日曜日は本を読んだり散歩したりします。
examples.reading: 日曜日は本を読んだり散歩したりします。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: On Sundays I read and take walks, among other things.

items.title: past plain + ことがあります
items.pattern: past plain + ことがあります
items.meaning: Say that someone has experienced an action before.
formation: past plain + ことがあります
notes: Say that someone has experienced an action before.

examples.japanese: 京都へ行ったことがあります。
examples.reading: 京都へ行ったことがあります。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: negative stem + なくてもいいです
items.pattern: negative stem + なくてもいいです
items.meaning: Say that an action is not required.
formation: negative stem + なくてもいいです
notes: Say that an action is not required.

examples.japanese: 明日は来なくてもいいです。
examples.reading: 明日は来なくてもいいです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: You do not have to come tomorrow.

items.title: plain past/negative + ほうがいいです
items.pattern: plain past/negative + ほうがいいです
items.meaning: Give gentle advice about a preferable action.
formation: plain past/negative + ほうがいいです
notes: Give gentle advice about a preferable action.

examples.japanese: 早く寝たほうがいいです。
examples.reading: 早く寝たほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: You should go to bed early.

items.title: Noun + だけ
items.meaning: Limit a statement to only the marked item or amount.
notes: Limit a statement to only the marked item or amount.

examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.

items.title: Noun + でも
items.meaning: Offer one representative option in a casual suggestion.
notes: Offer one representative option in a casual suggestion.

examples.japanese: お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.reading: お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: Would you like tea or something?

items.title: Sentence + ね
items.meaning: Invite agreement or acknowledge shared information.
notes: Invite agreement or acknowledge shared information.

examples.japanese: 今日はいい天気ですね。
examples.reading: 今日はいい天気ですね。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: The weather is nice, isn't it?

items.title: Sentence + よ
items.meaning: Present information the listener may not know.
notes: Present information the listener may not know.

examples.japanese: この電車は東京へ行きますよ。
examples.reading: この電車は東京へ行きますよ。
examples.romaji: See the Japanese reading in the lesson.
examples.translation: This train goes to Tokyo, you know.
